_comment: #1596: writer refusal is consumed by cpp:init and callers in other repositories without independently re-deriving whether replacement was allowed.
Inputs build owned scratch Node projects. Existing files and symlinks are asserted before invocation; a late file appears inside the actual generation phase.
The case driver tests the writer API, while end-to-end tests run the actual Tier4 snippet and real argparse CLI. No Node executable or third-party Python package is needed by this control.
The constructed anchor implements a plain write_text overwrite. It misses every BAD case and agrees on both GOOD cases. Its provenance is unverified.
Bounds: framework generation is source-derived; this does not execute or validate project lint/test commands.

cases.name: bad-existing
cases.why: An existing user Makefile must be refused and preserved without force.

cases.name: bad-symlink
cases.why: A user symlink is an existing entry; refusal must preserve both entry and target.

cases.name: bad-dangling-symlink
cases.why: A dangling symlink also exists; the guard must not create its target.

cases.name: bad-late-existing
cases.why: A competing Makefile appears during generation, after the initial guard; the atomic commit must refuse it.

cases.name: good-new-file
cases.why: A genuinely absent destination receives framework content, ruling out always-refuse blindness.

cases.name: good-explicit-force
cases.why: Explicit replacement must write framework content, the opposite of the default refusal.

anchors.why: A writer that generates correct content but ignores the overwrite guard. It gives a clean wrote result while replacing existing or late-created files and following symlinks.
